title: Make incremental memory synchronization proportional to changed keys and revisions
outcome: Incremental memory export selects and reads changed keys and their needed revisions rather than enumerating every project key and replaying every local history.
acceptance: An incremental memory export with an admitted changed-key basis does not enumerate or read unchanged keys or their unchanged revisions

The exported shared history and retirement/merge outcomes match the complete path for the operation's selected inputs, and an explicit complete export remains available with its documented reason and bound. Exact-byte checks cover files the operation reads or writes. Unrelated local edits remain unstaged and unpublished while the real incremental changes complete; publication stages only explicitly produced paths.

A mixed changed/unchanged history regression demonstrates Engram-side content reads, bytes, decodes and selected SQL work proportional to changed keys and needed revisions. It also proves a stray CRLF edit to an untouched revision is not published. Git-internal I/O is disclosed separately; no all-files scan, stat snapshot or environment-freeze guarantee is introduced.
